---
title: "Readings"
subtitle: "Fall 2026 required and recommended readings"
---

Readings are listed by class session. Complete the **Required** readings before class. Recommended readings are optional references for students who want additional depth or need them for the semester project.

## Access

- **Open access** links lead directly to material available without a subscription.
- **UT Libraries** links lead to the publisher or DOI record. Sign in through [UT Libraries](https://www.lib.utexas.edu/) when prompted. A course copy will also be posted on Canvas when permitted.
- Page ranges refer to the editions listed below. You are responsible only for the chapters, pages, or named sections specified.

## Core books

- Groves, Robert M., Floyd J. Fowler Jr., Mick P. Couper, James M. Lepkowski, Eleanor Singer, and Roger Tourangeau. 2009. *Survey Methodology*. 2nd ed. Wiley. [Book information](https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Survey+Methodology%2C+2nd+Edition-p-9780470465462). **UT Libraries/Canvas.**
- Dillman, Don A., Jolene D. Smyth, and Leah Melani Christian. 2014. *Internet, Phone, Mail, and Mixed-Mode Surveys: The Tailored Design Method*. 4th ed. Wiley. [Book information](https://www.wiley.com/en-us/Internet%2C%2BPhone%2C%2BMail%2C%2Band%2BMixed%2BMode%2BSurveys%3A%2BThe%2BTailored%2BDesign%2BMethod%2C%2B4th%2BEdition-p-9781118456149). **UT Libraries.**
- Marsden, Peter V., and James D. Wright, eds. 2010. *Handbook of Survey Research*. 2nd ed. Emerald. **Course PDF on Canvas.**
- Asher, Herbert. 2017. *Polling and the Public: What Every Citizen Should Know*. 9th ed. CQ Press. **Course PDF on Canvas.**
- Tourangeau, Roger, Lance J. Rips, and Kenneth Rasinski. 2000. *The Psychology of Survey Response*. Cambridge University Press. [Book information](https://doi.org/10.1017/CBO9780511819322). **UT Libraries/Canvas.**

Students are not expected to read these books cover to cover. Only the chapters or sections identified below are assigned.

## Session 1 · Polls, evidence, and error

**Required**

- American Association for Public Opinion Research (AAPOR). 2025. [“2024 Pre-Election Polling: An Evaluation of the 2024 General Election Polls,” Executive Summary](https://aapor.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/Task-Force-on-2024-Pre-Election-Polling-Report-Executive-Summary.pdf). Read the complete executive summary. **Open access.**
- AAPOR. [“Polling Accuracy.”](https://aapor.org/polling-accuracy/) Read the complete webpage. **Open access.**
- Groves et al. 2009. Chapter 2, “Inference and Error in Surveys,” pp. 39–64. **UT Libraries/Canvas.**

**Recommended**

- AAPOR. 2025. [Full report on 2024 pre-election polling](https://aapor.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/AAPOR-Task-Force-on-2024-Pre-Election-Polling_Report.pdf). **Open access.**
- Asher. 2017. Chapter 1, “Polling and the Public.” **Course PDF on Canvas.**

## Session 2 · Research objectives, ethics, and total survey error

**Required**

- AAPOR. [“Code of Professional Ethics and Practices.”](https://aapor.org/standards-and-ethics/) Read sections I–III: Principles of Professional Responsibility, Principles of Professional Practice in the Conduct of Our Work, and Standards for Disclosure. **Open access.**
- AAPOR. [“Best Practices for Survey Research.”](https://aapor.org/standards-and-ethics/best-practices/) Read the complete webpage. **Open access.**

**Recommended**

- AAPOR. [“Disclosure Standards.”](https://aapor.org/standards-and-ethics/disclosure-standards/) **Open access.**
- Groves et al. 2009. Re-read Chapter 2, pp. 48–64, focusing on Figure 2.5 and the individual components of total survey error. **UT Libraries/Canvas.**

## Session 3 · Concepts, measurement, and questionnaire architecture

**Required**

- Groves et al. 2009. Chapter 7, “Questions and Answers in Surveys,” pp. 217–253. Focus on the relationship among constructs, measurements, responses, and response error. **UT Libraries/Canvas.**
- Krosnick, Jon A., and Stanley Presser. 2010. [“Question and Questionnaire Design.”](https://www.betterevaluation.org/tools-resources/question-questionnaire-design) In *Handbook of Survey Research*, 2nd ed., pp. 263–313. Read pp. 263–286, through the end of the section on open versus closed questions. **Open-access resource page; course PDF on Canvas.**
- Pew Research Center. [“Writing Survey Questions.”](https://www.pewresearch.org/writing-survey-questions/) Read the sections “Question development,” “Measuring change over time,” and “Open- and closed-ended questions.” **Open access.**

**Recommended**

- Tourangeau, Rips, and Rasinski. 2000. Chapter 1, “The Psychology of Survey Response,” pp. 1–22. **UT Libraries/Canvas.**
- Converse, Jean M., and Stanley Presser. 1986. *Survey Questions: Handcrafting the Standardized Questionnaire*, Chapter 2, “The Logic of Survey Questions,” pp. 9–30. **UT Libraries.**

## Session 4 · Wording, response options, order, and sensitive questions

**Required**

- Schwarz, Norbert. 1999. [“Self-Reports: How the Questions Shape the Answers.”](https://doi.org/10.1037/0003-066X.54.2.93) *American Psychologist* 54(2): 93–105. Read the complete article. **UT Libraries.**
- Tourangeau, Roger, and Ting Yan. 2007. [“Sensitive Questions in Surveys.”](https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.133.5.859) *Psychological Bulletin* 133(5): 859–883. Read pp. 859–870 and the conclusion on pp. 878–879. **UT Libraries.**
- Pew Research Center. 2018. [“Methods 101: Survey Question Wording.”](https://www.pewresearch.org/methods/2018/03/21/methods-101-video-question-wording/) Watch the video and review the examples on the page. **Open access.**

**Recommended**

- Pew Research Center. 2019. [“When Online Survey Respondents Only ‘Select Some That Apply.’”](https://www.pewresearch.org/methods/2019/05/09/when-online-survey-respondents-only-select-some-that-apply/) **Open access.**
- Asher. 2017. Chapters 2–3, “The Problem of Nonattitudes” and “Wording and Context of Questions.” **Course PDF on Canvas.**
- Krosnick and Presser. 2010. Complete the remainder of Chapter 9 in the *Handbook of Survey Research*, pp. 287–313. **Course PDF on Canvas.**

## Session 5 · Cognitive testing and multilingual equivalence

**Required**

- Willis, Gordon B. 2005. *Cognitive Interviewing: A Tool for Improving Questionnaire Design*. Chapter 1, “An Introduction to Cognitive Interviewing,” pp. 1–15. **UT Libraries/Canvas.**
- Survey Research Center. 2016. [“Translation: Overview.”](https://ccsg.isr.umich.edu/chapters/translation/overview/) Read Guidelines 1–4 and their rationales. **Open access.**

**Recommended**

- Pan, Yuling, and Mandy Sha. 2019. *The Sociolinguistics of Survey Translation*, Chapter 2, “A Sociolinguistic Perspective on Survey Question Design and Translation,” pp. 21–39. **UT Libraries.**
- Willis, Gordon B. 2005. Chapter 4, “The Practice of Cognitive Interviewing,” pp. 42–65. **UT Libraries/Canvas.**
- Survey Research Center. 2016. [*Guidelines for Best Practice in Cross-Cultural Surveys*](https://ccsg.isr.umich.edu/wp-content/uploads/2019/06/CCSG_Full_Guidelines_2016_Version.pdf). Read “Pretesting: Cognitive Interviewing.” **Open access.**

## Session 6 · Sampling and representation

**Required**

- Groves et al. 2009. Chapter 3, “Target Populations, Sampling Frames, and Coverage Error,” pp. 69–94. **UT Libraries/Canvas.**
- Groves et al. 2009. Chapter 4, “Sample Design and Sampling Error,” pp. 97–118 only, stopping before “Systematic Sampling.” **UT Libraries/Canvas.**
- Pew Research Center. 2023. [“Comparing Two Types of Online Survey Samples.”](https://www.pewresearch.org/methods/2023/09/07/comparing-two-types-of-online-survey-samples/) Read the overview and “How the probability and opt-in samples compare.” **Open access.**

**Recommended**

- AAPOR. 2013. [“Report of the Task Force on Non-Probability Sampling.”](https://aapor.org/publications-resources/reports/) Open the report from the AAPOR reports page and read the executive summary. **Open access.**
- Kennedy, Courtney, et al. 2016. [“Evaluating Online Nonprobability Surveys.”](https://www.pewresearch.org/methods/2016/05/02/evaluating-online-nonprobability-surveys/) **Open access.**
- Asher. 2017. Chapter 4, “Sampling Techniques.” **Course PDF on Canvas.**

## Session 7 · Modes, recruitment, coverage, and nonresponse

**Required**

- Groves et al. 2009. Chapter 5, “Methods of Data Collection,” pp. 149–162, focusing on the comparison of survey modes. **UT Libraries/Canvas.**
- Pew Research Center. 2015. [“From Telephone to the Web: The Challenge of Mode-of-Interview Effects in Public Opinion Polls.”](https://www.pewresearch.org/methods/2015/05/13/from-telephone-to-the-web-the-challenge-of-mode-of-interview-effects-in-public-opinion-polls/) Read the overview and “Mode differences by question content.” **Open access.**

**Recommended**

- AAPOR. 2019. [“Transitions from Telephone Surveys to Self-Administered and Mixed-Mode Surveys.”](https://aapor.org/publications-resources/reports/) Open the report from the AAPOR reports page and read the executive summary. **Open access.**
- Groves, Robert M., and Emilia Peytcheva. 2008. [“The Impact of Nonresponse Rates on Nonresponse Bias.”](https://doi.org/10.1093/poq/nfn011) *Public Opinion Quarterly* 72(2): 167–189. Read pp. 167–181 and the conclusion on pp. 186–187. **UT Libraries.**
- Dillman, Smyth, and Christian. 2014. Chapter 11, “Mixed-Mode Questionnaires and Survey Implementation.” **UT Libraries.**
- Dillman and Benjamin Messer. 2010. Chapter 17, “Mixed-Mode Surveys,” in the *Handbook of Survey Research*, pp. 551–574. **Course PDF on Canvas.**

## Session 8 · Programming, mobile design, randomization, and QA

**Required**

- Dillman, Smyth, and Christian. 2014. Chapter 9, “Web Questionnaires and Implementation.” **UT Libraries.**
- U.S. Census Bureau. 2026. [*Design Guidelines for U.S. Census Bureau Web Surveys and Censuses*](https://www.census.gov/about/what/transformation/maximizing-operational-efficiency/data-centric-business-ecosystem/dice-overview/dice.html). Read “Overall Look and Feel,” “Screen Elements,” and the entries for single-select, multi-select, grids, and open-text questions under “Question Components.” **Open access.**
- **Course instrument QA protocol.** Read the complete checklist posted on Canvas and bring it to class. **Canvas.**

**Recommended**

- AAPOR. [“Disclosure Standards.”](https://aapor.org/standards-and-ethics/disclosure-standards/) Revisit as a design-stage audit tool. **Open access.**
- Martin, Elizabeth, et al. 2007. [“Guidelines for Designing Questionnaires for Administration in Different Modes.”](https://www.census.gov/library/working-papers/2007/adrm/rsm2007-42.html) Read the introduction and Guidelines 1–12. **Open access.**
- Couper, Mick P., and Michael Bosnjak. 2010. Chapter 16, “Internet Surveys,” in the *Handbook of Survey Research*, pp. 527–550. **Course PDF on Canvas.**

## Session 9 · Fieldwork, paradata, fraud, and respondent quality

**Required**

- Dillman, Smyth, and Christian. 2014. Chapter 2, “Reducing People’s Reluctance to Respond to Surveys,” pp. 19–55. **UT Libraries.**
- AAPOR. 2022. [*Data Quality Metrics for Online Samples: Considerations for Study Design and Analysis*](https://aapor.org/wp-content/uploads/2023/02/Task-Force-Report-FINAL.pdf). Read Section 1, “Introduction and Scope,” pp. 1–2, and Section 6, “Summary and Recommendations,” pp. 49–51. **Open access.**
- Kennedy, Courtney, et al. 2020. [*Assessing the Risks to Online Polls From Bogus Respondents*](https://www.pewresearch.org/methods/wp-content/uploads/sites/10/2020/02/PM_02.18.20_dataquality_FULL.REPORT.pdf). Read the overview, pp. 2–8, and the report’s concluding recommendations. **Open access.**

**Recommended**

- Pew Research Center. 2020. [“Answers That Did Not Match the Question Were Concentrated in Opt-In Polls.”](https://www.pewresearch.org/methods/2020/02/18/answers-that-did-not-match-the-question-were-concentrated-in-opt-in-polls/) **Open access.**
- AAPOR. 2020. [“Falsification in Surveys.”](https://aapor.org/publications-resources/reports/) Open the report from the AAPOR reports page and read the executive summary and recommendations. **Open access.**

## Session 10 · Cleaning, coding, weighting, and documentation

**Required**

- Pew Research Center. 2018. [“For Weighting Online Opt-In Samples, What Matters Most?”](https://www.pewresearch.org/methods/2018/01/26/for-weighting-online-opt-in-samples-what-matters-most/) Read the overview and conclusion. **Open access.**
- Pew Research Center. 2018. [“How Different Weighting Methods Work.”](https://www.pewresearch.org/methods/2018/01/26/how-different-weighting-methods-work/) Read the complete methods explainer. **Open access.**

**Recommended**

- Lumley, Thomas. 2010. *Complex Surveys: A Guide to Analysis Using R*, Chapter 1, “Basic Tools,” pp. 1–14. **UT Libraries/Canvas.**
- Groves et al. 2009. Chapter 10, “Postcollection Processing of Survey Data,” pp. 343–365. **UT Libraries/Canvas.**

## Session 11 · Estimation, uncertainty, and subgroup analysis

**Required**

- Pew Research Center. 2021. [“Why Pew Research Center Will Display Margins of Error in Some Graphics.”](https://www.pewresearch.org/decoded/2021/10/25/why-pew-research-center-will-display-margins-of-error-in-some-graphics/) Read the complete explainer. **Open access.**
- Pew Research Center. 2018. [“Variability of Survey Estimates.”](https://www.pewresearch.org/methods/2018/01/26/variability-of-survey-estimates/) Read the complete methods explainer. **Open access.**
- Wasserstein, Ronald L., Allen L. Schirm, and Nicole A. Lazar. 2019. [“Moving to a World Beyond ‘p < 0.05.’”](https://doi.org/10.1080/00031305.2019.1583913) *The American Statistician* 73(sup1): 1–19. Read pp. 1–10. **Open access.**

**Recommended**

- Lumley, Thomas. 2010. *Complex Surveys*, Chapter 2, “Simple and Stratified Sampling,” pp. 15–31. **UT Libraries/Canvas.**

## Session 12 · Visualization and public interpretation

**Required**

- Healy, Kieran. 2018. [*Data Visualization: A Practical Introduction*](https://socviz.co/). Read Chapter 1, “Look at Data.” **Open access.**

**Recommended**

- Cairo, Alberto. 2019. *How Charts Lie*, Chapter 2, “How Charts Lie: Poor Design,” pp. 23–49. **UT Libraries/Canvas.**
- Healy, Kieran. 2018. Chapter 2, “Get Started.” **Open access.**
- Schwabish, Jonathan A. 2021. *Better Data Visualizations*. Chapter 2, “Five Guidelines for Better Data Visualizations,” pp. 17–42. **UT Libraries/Canvas.**
- AAPOR. [“Disclosure Standards.”](https://aapor.org/standards-and-ethics/disclosure-standards/) Read sections 1–3. **Open access.**
- **Applied comparison:** The two polling releases named on Canvas. **Canvas.**

## Session 13 · Reporting, peer review, and partner briefing

**Required preparation:** No new reading. Bring the complete team draft and apply the course report style guide and reproducibility checklist before class.

**Recommended reference while revising**

- AAPOR. [“Transparency Initiative.”](https://aapor.org/standards-and-ethics/transparency-initiative/) Review “What must be disclosed?” **Open access.**
- Pew Research Center. [“Writing Survey Questions.”](https://www.pewresearch.org/writing-survey-questions/) Review how the page documents question wording and order. **Open access.**
- Asher. 2017. Chapters 6 and 9, “The Media and the Polls” and “Polling and Democracy,” especially “How to Evaluate Polls: A Summary.” **Course PDF on Canvas.**

## Session 14 · Presentation and retrospective

There is no new reading. Review the final report, peer feedback, decision log, and your individual contribution record before class.
